attempts.narrative: Led Incineroar + Rillaboom. T1 I aimed Fake Out at Raikou and it did nothing: Raikou's ability is Inner Focus, so the authored lead is deliberately Fake-Out-proof and my opening was simply wrong. Raikou's Thunderbolt and Infernape's Close Combat (2x into Fire/Dark) then took Incineroar from 148 to 24 through the Sitrus in a single turn, while Rillaboom's High Horsepower left Infernape on 1 HP behind its Focus Sash. T2 I switched Incineroar out for Weavile, which was my real error - Weavile is 4x weak to Fighting and Infernape's Mach Punch plus Raikou's Thunderbolt removed it immediately. Rillaboom's Grassy Glide finished Infernape. T3 Togekiss came in, Rillaboom's Wood Hammer KO'd Raikou and a critical Air Slash KO'd Exeggutor before it ever chose a move. T4 Blastoise Mega Evolved, used Water Pulse into Togekiss, and Rillaboom's Wood Hammer (2x) ended it.

strategy_checks.check: Infernape's Fake Out supports immediate Raikou offense
strategy_checks.result: NOT OBSERVED, and the plan line is questionable
strategy_checks.evidence: Infernape never used Fake Out. On T1 it chose Close Combat into Incineroar for 2x, which was clearly the better action - Incineroar had just Intimidated it and was the only target Fake Out could have flinched, and Fake Out into a Pokemon that was about to be removed anyway is worth less than 99 damage. On T2 it used Mach Punch from 1 HP behind its Sash and got a KO on the switch-in. Both choices are correct; what this shows is that the authored plan's headline tactic is the weakest thing Infernape can do with this moveset.

strategy_checks.check: Exeggutor supplies Sleep Powder and Sitrus/Harvest recovery
strategy_checks.evidence: Exeggutor came in on T3 and was KO'd by a critical Air Slash (2x into Grass/Psychic) before it selected an action. No fault of the AI; the check simply never got a board.

strategy_checks.check: Blastoise Mega Evolves in slot 4 and uses Mega Launcher pulse coverage
strategy_checks.evidence: T4: 'The opposing Blastoise has Mega Evolved', immediately followed by Water Pulse into Togekiss for 40. The Mega fired on the first turn it was legal and it picked a pulse move, which is the Mega Launcher payoff the plan names. Target choice was right too: Togekiss was on 53 HP and Rillaboom was behind an Assault Vest.

strategy_checks.check: Raikou selects attacks rather than unnecessary support when ahead
strategy_checks.evidence: Raikou used Thunderbolt on all three of its turns and never reached for Snarl or Protect while it was ahead on board. Life Orb recoil was accepted each time. That is exactly the 'select attacks instead of unnecessary support' line.

strategy_checks.check: Inner Focus on the Electric ace
strategy_checks.result: PASS, and it is the best-designed detail in the team
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Fake Out into Raikou produced no flinch. Raikou is the fastest and most dangerous member and it is specifically immune to the single most common doubles opening. A player who does not read the set loses a turn, which is what happened to me.

protect_ledger_note: Zero opposing Protects in four turns, across three Pokemon that carry it (Raikou, Exeggutor, Blastoise). Nothing to criticise: the AI was ahead or even on board the whole time and attacked every turn, which is what the plan asks for. Exeggutor and Blastoise each had only one live turn.
ai_notes: No illegal or nonsensical choice in this battle. Every opponent action was the best or near-best available: Close Combat over Fake Out into a soon-dead Incineroar, Mach Punch from 1 HP into a 4x-weak switch-in, Thunderbolt every turn, and a first-legal-turn Mega Evolution into the correct pulse.

The Mach Punch on T2 deserves specific credit. Infernape was on 1 HP behind a spent Sash, facing a fresh switch-in; it picked the priority move that was 4x on the incoming Ice/Dark and got the KO before dying. That is a switch-in read from the board, not a habit.

The plan text oversells Fake Out. Infernape correctly refused to use it twice, so the authored sentence 'Infernape's Fake Out can support immediate Raikou offense' describes a line the AI itself evaluates as worse than attacking. That is a documentation mismatch, not a defect.

could_this_be_cooler: Yes, in one specific way, and it is not a species swap. The four pieces are individually excellent and the Inner Focus Raikou is a genuinely clever anti-metagame detail, but the team has no interaction between its members - Raikou, Infernape, Exeggutor and Blastoise never help each other do anything. It is four good Pokemon standing next to each other, which for an Ace on the road to the Heat Badge is a step below what the rest of this block manages (Shayla's Storm Drain Surf, Georgia's Weakness Policy activation, Lawrence's sand). The cheapest fix that keeps every species is to give the plan a real connective tissue: Exeggutor already carries Sleep Powder and a Sitrus, and Harvest plus sun would make it a recurring berry engine - Infernape could be the sun, or Exeggutor could hold the redirection instead. As authored, Harvest is the plan's own admission that something is missing ('Harvest is not guaranteed without actual sun'). I would not replace Raikou or Blastoise; I would make Exeggutor's slot do something for its partners.
